blocks.md: A token bucket turns a steady refill rate into a controlled burst allowance. Requests spend tokens; virtual time earns them back, but the bucket never grows beyond `Burst`.

blocks.label: FIG 1
blocks.caption: No timer updates the bucket in the background. Each request first accounts for elapsed virtual time, then makes one deterministic decision.

blocks.title: Keep fractional refill
blocks.md: The rate is rational: `RateNum / RateDen`. Preserve the remainder between requests or repeated small time steps will refill more slowly than one equivalent large step.

blocks.input:
rate = 2 tokens / 3 ticks
burst = 4, tokens = 1
request: cost 3 at tick 3
blocks.output:
refill 2 → tokens 3
Allowed = true, tokens left = 0
blocks.explain: Three elapsed ticks earn exactly two tokens. If only one token were available, `RetryAt` would be the first later tick where accumulated refill reaches the missing amount.

items: Use checked integer arithmetic; do not use floating point or wall time.
Zero refill, zero burst, and cost above burst can make a positive-cost request impossible forever.
Same-tick requests receive no refill between decisions.

items.title: Normalize configuration
items.md: Treat a zero denominator as one and initialize the bucket at Burst.

items.title: Refill lazily
items.md: Convert elapsed ticks into whole tokens while carrying fractional remainder and clamping capacity.

items.title: Invert the rate
items.md: For rejection, solve how many ticks are needed to earn the missing tokens and round up safely.

blocks.title: Optimization target
blocks.md: Once decisions and `RetryAt` are exact, reduce repeated arithmetic and allocation. Throughput rewards the fast path; `arithmetic_work` makes avoidable recomputation visible.
